own.lead: Owlat manages the DNS for you.
own.records: The SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records shown for each domain below are the managed records — add them exactly as displayed, then verify.
own.signing: Once verified, Owlat signs your mail as your domain automatically.

api.lead: Your provider verifies this domain through its own identity API.
api.records: Publish the SPF and DKIM records your provider shows for this domain, exactly as displayed.
api.verification: Then complete the provider’s own domain verification. Until that clears, it can reject mail from this domain no matter how good the DNS is.
api.dmarc: Keep a DMARC record on the domain so receivers can check that SPF or DKIM aligns; your existing policy stays authoritative.

none.lead: Your provider handles SPF and DKIM for you.
none.setupGuide: Follow your provider’s setup guide to add their SPF include and DKIM records for this domain.
none.confirm: Then confirm two things: your domain’s SPF authorizes the provider, and mail from it carries a DKIM signature that validates for your domain.

ses.lead: SES signs your mail with its own DKIM identity tokens.
ses.dkim: In the SES console, open Verified identities → your domain → and add the three DKIM CNAME records SES generates for the identity.
ses.spf: Keep an SPF record that authorizes SES (include amazonses.com) and a DMARC record so receivers can check alignment.

smtp.lead: Your relay provider handles SPF and DKIM for you.
smtp.setupGuide: Follow your provider’s setup guide to add their SPF include and DKIM records for this domain.
smtp.confirm: Then confirm two things: your domain’s SPF authorizes the relay, and mail from the relay carries a DKIM signature that validates for your domain.

resend.lead: Resend signs your mail once your domain is verified there.
resend.records: In the Resend dashboard, add the SPF and DKIM records it shows for this domain.
resend.dmarc: A DMARC record on top lets receivers check that SPF or DKIM aligns with your domain.

mandrill.lead: Mailchimp Transactional signs with one shared key, so your records are the same every time.
mandrill.records: Publish the two records shown under “Mailchimp Transactional sending domains” below: the SPF include that authorizes Mandrill’s IPs, and the DKIM TXT at mandrill._domainkey. They are derived from your domain name, so they are exactly what Owlat registered.
mandrill.verification: Then complete Mandrill’s own domain verification — the TXT token shown beside the records, or the confirmation flow in Settings → Domains → Sending Domains. Until that clears, Mandrill rejects mail from this domain no matter how good the DNS is.
mandrill.dmarc: Keep a DMARC record on the domain so receivers can check that SPF or DKIM aligns; your existing policy stays authoritative.

descriptions.mta: Owlat’s built-in mail server sends your mail directly and manages IP warm-up.
descriptions.ses: Mail goes out through your Amazon SES account.
descriptions.resend: Mail goes out through your Resend account.
descriptions.smtp: Mail is handed to your SMTP relay, which delivers it on your behalf.
descriptions.mandrill: Mail goes out through your Mailchimp Transactional (Mandrill) account, so you keep the reputation you arrived with.
descriptions.generic: Mail goes out through {transport}. Check that transport’s authentication setup before sending.
